$comment: What the OpenAPI document cannot say, each entry with where it came from.
constants become fields of the generated JevContract class, so the runtime reads them from here rather than
from a literal of its own. basis is one of: documented (a TypeSafe documentation page says so), observed (seen
on the wire, dated), decision (nothing upstream settles it; this SDK chose, and the note says why).
conflicts record where TypeSafe's own descriptions of the API differ. Each carries checks against openapi.json: if a later
snapshot stops saying what a resolution relies on, generation stops and the resolution has to be revisited.
Everything here was verified on 2026-09-23 against info.version 0.2.0. The base address, the choice and score limits and
status 400 were revisited on 2026-10-24, when the snapshot retrieved that day (still info.version 0.2.0) began to declare them.

constants.name: defaultBaseAddress
constants.note: The origin every documented request goes to, and the one server the OpenAPI document names (servers, since the snapshot retrieved 2026-10-24). The generator stops if the document names any other.

constants.name: defaultModel
constants.note: A moving alias: 'the most recent stable, official release'. Convenient, and not reproducible; pin a versioned id such as jev-1.13.0 when results have to be comparable over time.

constants.name: choiceOptionsMaximum
constants.note: 'You can have a maximum of 255 options per Choice.' The OpenAPI document declares the same maximum since the snapshot retrieved 2026-10-24; see the conflict choice-and-score-limits.

constants.name: choiceOptionsMinimum
constants.note: No source states a minimum. Zero options can never produce an answer, so they are refused; one is the smallest request nothing rules out, and is accepted even though it can only ever select itself. The OpenAPI document declares minProperties 1 since the snapshot retrieved 2026-10-24, which agrees.

constants.name: scoreLevelsMaximum
constants.note: 'A Score should have at least two levels; the API accepts up to 10.' The OpenAPI document declares the same maximum since the snapshot retrieved 2026-10-24; see the conflict choice-and-score-limits.

constants.name: scoreLevelsMinimum
constants.note: The OpenAPI document requires one level, and the HTTP reference says a Score should have at least two. A one-level score can only ever answer 0 with probability 1, so this SDK refuses it.

constants.name: requestIdHeader
sources: Observed on every response, including 401 and 403, on 2026-09-23: req_ followed by 32 hex digits
constants.note: The only response header the SDK reads besides Retry-After. Kept only when it is at most 128 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_-].

constants.name: retryAfterMillisecondsHeader
constants.note: Not in the HTTP reference, which asks for exponential backoff on 429 and 529, and not yet seen on a real 429. Read when present, before Retry-After, because it is the more precise of the two; without either, the SDK's own backoff applies.

constants.name: overloadedStatus
constants.note: 'TypeSafe is temporarily overloaded. Retry after a short delay.' Not a registered HTTP status; see the conflict status-529-undeclared.

conflicts.summary: The HTTP reference marks instructions required on every question type. The OpenAPI document makes it optional and nullable on all three.

sources.says: instructions is absent from 'required' on NoulQuestion, ChoiceQuestion and ScoreQuestion, and its anyOf includes null
instructions: string | object | array, required
a noul question without instructions was answered with 200

conflicts.resolution: Follow the OpenAPI document, which is what the service publishes as its own validation schema and what the service was seen to accept. The builder omits instructions for default(JevContent) and writes null for JevContent.Null.

conflicts.summary: The OpenAPI document requires one score level. The HTTP reference says a Score should have at least two.

sources.says: ScoreQuestion.criteria minItems 1
A Score should have at least two levels
a one-level score was answered with 200: score 0.0, probability 1.0 on its only level

conflicts.resolution: The SDK requires two (constant scoreLevelsMinimum). The service accepts one, but a one-level score can only ever answer that level, so it carries no information.

conflicts.summary: The HTTP reference types the score legend as map<string, string>. The OpenAPI document admits strings, objects and arrays, and the documentation shows a structured legend coming back.

sources.says: ScoreAnswer.legend values are anyOf string, object, array
legend: map<string, string>
a response whose legend values are objects with 'what' and 'examples'
levels sent as an object, an object and an array came back in the legend exactly as sent

conflicts.resolution: Legend values are held as JSON, never narrowed to strings.

conflicts.summary: The HTTP reference types Noul criteria descriptions as string, object or array. The OpenAPI document also admits null.

sources.says: NoulCriteria.true and NoulCriteria.false are optional, anyOf string, object, array, null
true: string | object | array; false: string | object | array

conflicts.resolution: Each side may be omitted, null or a value, independently.

conflicts.summary: The HTTP reference limits a Choice to 255 options and a Score to 10 levels. The OpenAPI document declared neither limit until the snapshot retrieved 2026-10-24, which declares both with the same values.

sources.says: maxProperties 255 on ChoiceQuestion.criteria and maxItems 10 on ScoreQuestion.criteria, since the snapshot retrieved 2026-10-24; neither before
a maximum of 255 options per Choice; the API accepts up to 10 levels
256 options and 11 levels were each refused with 400 and a plain string detail: 'Too many choices. Must have at most 255 choices.', 'Too many score levels. Must have at most 10 levels.'

conflicts.resolution: Enforced before sending, from the documented values (constants choiceOptionsMaximum and scoreLevelsMaximum). The document now states the same two values. The checks pin them, and the generator reads a maximum only where a check pins it, so a change to either value stops generation until the constants are revisited.

conflicts.summary: The HTTP reference answers a missing or invalid API key with 401. Observed: a missing key answers 403, an invalid one 401. Neither status is in the OpenAPI document.

sources.says: 401 Unauthorized: Missing or invalid API key

sources.url: Observed 2026-09-23 without a key and with a malformed one
sources.says: 403 {"detail":{"error_type":"authentication_error",...}} without a key; 401 with the same body shape for an invalid key

conflicts.resolution: Neither is retried. The SDK refuses to send a request without a usable key, so a 403 it reports is the service refusing a key it was given.

conflicts.summary: The service answers 400 for a request it understands but will not serve. The HTTP reference does not list 400. The OpenAPI document did not either until the snapshot retrieved 2026-10-24, which declares it with a detail that is a string or an object, the two shapes observed.

sources.says: responses 200, 400 (HTTPBadRequestError, whose detail is a string or an object) and 422, since the snapshot retrieved 2026-10-24; 200 and 422 only before
an unknown model: 400 {"detail":{"error_type":"api_usage_error","message":...}}; too many options or levels: 400 with a string detail

conflicts.resolution: 400 is not retried: the same request would be refused again. api_usage_error is a known error type and appears in the exception message; the server's message, which names the model, does not. The declared detail is what the error reader already takes apart: an object yields its error type, a string yields nothing.

conflicts.summary: The HTTP reference documents 529 Overloaded. The OpenAPI document lists only 200 and 422.

sources.says: 529 Overloaded: TypeSafe is temporarily overloaded. Retry after a short delay.
responses 200 and 422 only

conflicts.resolution: 529 is kept as a retry candidate (constant overloadedStatus). Retrying stays opt-in.
